blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Field errors are conveyed by colour only) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-accessibility-2 (Removing the error summary leaves no announced feedback on submit) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
`field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed, since the red border already shows where the problem
is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: Keep the red border as a supplement only: render a text message next to each invalid field (e.g. "Enter a valid postcode"), tie it to the input with `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input. Screen reader users and colour-blind users cannot otherwise tell a field is invalid nor why (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification, 3.3.3 Error Suggestion, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value).
findings.title: Field errors are conveyed by colour only

findings.evidence: - The error list at the top of the form is removed.
findings.recommendation: Specify what happens when the customer submits with invalid fields: either keep an error summary (focused on submit, each entry linking to its field) or move focus to the first invalid field whose error text is announced. Blur-only validation with no message and no summary leaves keyboard and screen reader users unable to find or understand the blocking error (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 2.4.3 Focus Order, 4.1.3 Status Messages).
findings.title: Removing the error summary leaves no announced feedback on submit

findings.recommendation: Add THEN clauses that require a text error message next to the field, programmatically associated with it (`aria-describedby`) and `aria-invalid` set, and its removal in "A corrected field"; tasks 1.2 tests would then check what assistive technology receives, not only a CSS class (WCAG 3.3.1, 1.3.1 Info and Relationships).
findings.title: Spec scenarios only verify the border colour
